record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: What is the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the topological-conjugacy relation for Axiom A dynamical systems?

evidence.quote: Question 1.4 (Foreman). What is the complexity of the relation of topological conjugacy of Axiom A systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$-diffeomorphisms of $M$. A diffeomorphism $f\in\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is said to satisfy Smale's Axiom A if its non-wandering set $\Omega(f)$ is hyperbolic and the periodic points of $f$ are dense in $\Omega(f)$. Two diffeomorphisms $f,g\in\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon M\to M$ with $h\circ f = g\circ h$. This determines an equivalence relation $\cong_{TC}$ on the Borel subset $A(M)\subseteq\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ of Axiom A diffeomorphisms.

Determine the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the equivalence relation $\cong_{TC}$ on $A(M)$ in the sense of Borel reducibility: in particular, locate this equivalence relation within the hierarchy of Borel/analytic equivalence relations (e.g., whether it is Borel, classifiable by countable structures, reducible to an orbit equivalence relation of a Polish group action, or universal among such relations).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has determined the Borel complexity of topological conjugacy in related settings — Cantor minimal systems, Toeplitz subshifts, invertible chaotic systems on the Cantor space, and diffeomorphisms on manifolds of dimension at least 2 (shown not classifiable by countable structures). However, no source located pinpoints the precise Borel-reducibility complexity of topological conjugacy specifically restricted to the class of Axiom A systems, so the status of this specific question appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Classification complexity of chaotic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Topological conjugacy of invertible chaotic systems on Cantor space has complexity of a universal orbit equivalence relation; diffeomorphisms on manifolds of dim ≥ 2 not classifiable by countable structures.
status_evidence.claim: Related complexity questions of Foreman/Gorodetski resolved, but Axiom A case not specifically addressed.

status_evidence.title: The complexity of the Structure and Classification of Dynamical Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Borel complexity results for conjugacy relations in dynamical systems.
status_evidence.claim: No definitive resolution stated for Axiom A topological conjugacy.
